sections.overview: Dorcadion scopolii is a flightless longhorn beetle in the family Cerambycidae, recorded across parts of central and eastern Europe.
sections.identification: Adults are about 10–13 mm long; the species is placed in the subgenus Cribridorcadion.
sections.habitat: Records and regional accounts place it in low vegetation and grassland settings, including Hungarian steppe meadows.
sections.diet: The species account lists grass roots as a food resource, without detailing the diet by life stage.
sections.behavior: Adults are reported from April to June and are usually found walking among low vegetation rather than flying.
sections.reproduction: The species has a one-year life cycle in the regional account; the finer details of mating and egg-laying were not established by the sources consulted.
sections.ecology: As a grass-associated beetle, it is linked to open ground vegetation; the consulted sources do not establish a narrower ecological requirement.
sections.conservation: The consulted species accounts provide no global conservation category; regional occurrence records should not be treated as a global status assessment.
